content.text:
View A represents four objects: upper is a yellow cross, right is a green circle, lower is a red triangle, and left is a blue square. Attention is currently concentrated on the left (blue square). Despite low immediate selection for the other three, the lower (red triangle) is the most recoverable if attention shifts away, followed by the upper (yellow cross) and then the right (green circle), which is least recoverable. Predicted outcomes of explicit selection commands show strong control: issuing a command to a given location reliably redirects selection to that location, so the system can reliably move attention from the left to any other location.

View B also contains four objects: upper is a yellow cross, right is a green triangle, lower is a red circle, and left is a blue square. Attention is currently concentrated on the left (blue square). The right and upper objects are moderately recoverable if attention moves; the lower (red circle) is least recoverable. Predicted effects of selection commands are similar regardless of which location is requested: commands tend to drive attention to the upper location, so the system has little control to redirect attention away from the upper bias.
